Bills mailed once a year; Treasurer page says taxes due 3rd Monday in August.. See the official page.

Las Vegas by the numbers

Which county bills property tax for a Las Vegas house?

Clark County does. Las Vegas is the county seat of Clark County, and the County Assessor values the property while the County Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

The Clark County Treasurer is at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1220, phone (702) 455-4323. The office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and closed Friday through Sunday. Mailing address changes go to the County Assessor on a form the county provides.

How big is Las Vegas and how did it start?

Las Vegas is the most populous city in Nevada, with 641,903 residents in the 2020 census. The metropolitan area has an estimated 2.4 million residents. The city covers 135.86 square miles, almost all of it land, at an elevation of about 2,030 feet.

The city was settled in 1905, when 110 acres next to the Union Pacific Railroad tracks were auctioned in what became downtown, and it was incorporated on March 16, 1911. Fremont Street is named for the explorer John C. Frémont, who arrived in 1844. Between 1990 and 2000 the population grew by 85.2%.

Not every address people call Las Vegas is inside the city. Paradise, Spring Valley, Enterprise and Summerlin South are unincorporated, while Henderson, North Las Vegas and Boulder City are separate incorporated cities. All of them still pay property tax through the same Clark County offices, so the process below fits each.

How does the desert climate affect a Las Vegas house?

Las Vegas has a hot desert climate with long, extremely hot summers, short winters with cool nights, and about 310 sunny days a year. The highest official temperature, 120 degrees F, was recorded at Harry Reid International Airport on July 7, 2024.

Annual precipitation averages only 4.18 inches, with most of it in winter, and snow in the city is rare. Long stretches of extreme heat are hard on roofs, cooling equipment and exterior finishes, so those are the items a buyer's inspector is likely to check first.

Water is the other local theme. Daily water consumption fell from about 314 gallons per resident in 2003 to about 205 gallons in 2015, and conservation efforts include a movement to encourage xeriscapes and scheduled watering days for residential landscaping.

When is Las Vegas property tax due?

Taxes are payable in four installments. The Clark County Treasurer lists them as the third Monday in August, the first Monday in October, the first Monday in January and the first Monday in March, with the fiscal year running July 1 to June 30. If the total for the year is $100 or less, it must be paid on the first installment.

Bills are mailed only once each fiscal year. If one has not arrived by August 1, the county says to use its automated phone system to request a copy, which is sent to the address on record. A ten-day grace period applies, and a payment must be received or postmarked within 10 calendar days of the due date.

Postage matters. The county counts standard stamps with a postmark, but metered mail, pre-canceled stamps, Automated Postal Center stamps and permit imprints carry no postmark, so a late-arriving envelope with one of those is treated as late.

After the grace period the penalties are:

  • 4% when one installment is unpaid
  • An added 5% when two are unpaid
  • An added 6% when three are unpaid
  • A 7% penalty when all four are late

How can I pay Clark County property tax?

The county accepts payment online, by phone, by mail, in person and through a bank's bill pay. E-check payments online or by phone carry no fee, while debit and credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, Discover) carry a service fee charged by a third-party provider. The automated phone line is (702) 455-4323, option 1.

In person, payments go to the first floor of the County Government Center, behind security, and cash, check and debit cards are accepted there without a fee. A drop box on the southwest side of the building takes checks only. Mailed checks are made payable to the Clark County Treasurer, with parcel numbers and payment coupons included. Email and text reminders are also offered.

What happens if Las Vegas property tax goes unpaid?

Delinquent properties are advertised, and after three years the county can take the title as trustee for a tax auction. The Treasurer says properties with taxes not paid in full at the end of April are advertised as delinquent in the local newspaper and on the Treasurer's website. The notice for the 2023 to 2024 year listed properties delinquent as of May 1, 2024.

The path from there is spelled out in NRS 361.585 and 361.590 according to the county. Property delinquent for three consecutive fiscal years is deeded into the name of the Clark County Treasurer as trustee, and a property found abandoned for two consecutive fiscal years may also be deeded to the Treasurer. Once that happens, it can be auctioned.

Key points the county gives about its auctions:

  • At least one auction per year, usually in spring, with a possible second in fall.
  • Properties are sold as is, all sales are final, and there is no redemption period for the buyer.
  • The previous owner has a two-year period to protest the sale.
  • The minimum bid covers taxes, penalties, interest and costs, and can include sanitation, sewer, special improvement district and nuisance abatement charges.
  • Any money above the minimum bid is excess proceeds, and the claim must be made within one year after the deed is recorded.

Paying the tax before the property reaches that stage keeps the house in the owner's hands. Special improvement district assessments run on a separate track, with their own delinquency sales held four times a year.

How do I challenge a Las Vegas property assessment?

Ask the Assessor's appraiser to review the value first. If that does not work, a petition to the Clark County Board of Equalization must be filed with the Assessor by January 15, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or holiday. The next level is the State Board of Equalization, then District Court.

Nevada limits how much a bill can rise through abatements. Owner-occupied single-family primary residences are held to a 3% increase over the prior year's tax, and other property falls under a general abatement of up to 8%. The caps do not apply to a property in its first year after new improvements or after a change of use. Assessed value is 35% of taxable value, and the combined tax rate is capped at $3.66 per $100 of assessed value.

Rates differ by tax district within Clark County. The Treasurer publishes rate tables by district and by entity, so use the one for your parcel instead of a citywide figure.

What transfer costs apply when a Las Vegas house sells?

The Real Property Transfer Tax in Clark County is $2.55 per $500 of value, which is the $1.95 statewide base plus $0.60 added in Clark County. The County Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded, and a Declaration of Value form is required for documents that convey an interest in real property.

The Department of Taxation gives an example for a $100,500 property in Clark County. The base tax is $393.90, the Clark County add-on is $120.60, and the total is $514.50. Buyer and seller are both liable for the tax.

The statute lists exemptions, including transfers to or from a trust without consideration and a deed upon death under NRS 111.109. If you are not sure whether yours qualifies, the Recorder reviews exemption applications.

If you are behind on property tax or a special assessment, the title company will pull a payoff and pay it from your proceeds. Cash Home Buyers buys Las Vegas houses as-is, so there is no repair or listing prep before closing. Verify all amounts with the Clark County Treasurer and Recorder, since fees and dates are reset each fiscal year.

More questions about Las Vegas, NV Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay property tax to in Las Vegas, NV?

The Clark County Treasurer, at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, Las Vegas. The County Assessor values the property. You can pay online, by phone at (702) 455-4323, by mail, or in person Monday through Thursday.

When are Las Vegas property taxes due?

In four installments on the third Monday in August and the first Monday in October, January and March. A ten-day grace period applies, and taxes of $100 or less for the year are due with the first installment.

What is the penalty for paying Las Vegas property tax late?

After the grace period, the penalty is 4% for one unpaid installment, with added penalties of 5%, 6% and 7% as two, three or all four installments go unpaid.

What is the appeal deadline for a Las Vegas assessment?

January 15, filed with the Clark County Assessor, or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday. The appeal goes to the Clark County Board of Equalization.

How much is transfer tax on a Las Vegas home sale?

The Clark County rate is $2.55 per $500 of value. On a $100,500 transfer, the Department of Taxation's example total is $514.50.

Can the county auction my Las Vegas house for unpaid tax?

Yes, in time. Property delinquent for three consecutive fiscal years is deeded to the Clark County Treasurer as trustee, after which it can be sold at auction. Paying the tax or selling the house earlier avoids that.
